result.question:
I want to set the next oil sampling date for Transformer 1 at site MAIN based on how fast the gases are actually growing, not on a fixed calendar.

Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out TDCG for every sample. Use only hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co, and leave out co2, oxygen and nitrogen. Give me the TDCG rate in ppm/day between the first and last sample, and name the gas that contributes most to the increase.

Before trusting that rate, screen the six gases for anomalous samples. If a single anomalous sample is driving the rise, recompute the rate without it and show me both numbers.

Set the interval with this rule:
- Under 10 ppm/day: next sample in 90 days.
- 10 to 30 ppm/day: next sample in 30 days.
- Above 30 ppm/day: next sample in 7 days.

If the rate with and without the anomalous sample lands in different bands, don't escalate on the higher one. Use the lower band's interval and add a confirmatory resample within 7 days to settle it.

Also run a fault classification on the latest complete sample. If it comes back D1, D2 or T3, use 7 days no matter what the rate says.

Then check open work orders on Transformer 1. If a sampling job is already open, don't create another. Tell me its number and date, and whether it should move earlier. Otherwise, pick the first day on or after the target date where MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders, create the sampling work order for that day, and assign a technician who has sampled Transformer 1 before.

If fewer than two samples in the window have all six gases, say the rate can't be computed. In that case, base the interval on the classification alone: 7 days for D1, D2 or T3, and 30 days otherwise.
result.answer:
The next sample should be **90 days out, around 2026-12-29**. Transformer 1 already has an open sampling job, **WO 1000052**, targeted for **2026-10-01**, so I didn't create another one and it doesn't need to move earlier.

**TDCG per sample (H₂ + CH₄ + C₂H₆ + C₂H₄ + C₂H₂ + CO)**

| Sample | H₂ | CH₄ | C₂H₆ | C₂H₄ | C₂H₂ | CO | TDCG (ppm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 | 32,441 |
| 2024-01-16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 30 | 32,086 |
| 2024-01-17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 35 | 32,343 |
| 2024-01-18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 | 32,340 |

All four samples have all six gases, so the rate can be computed.

- **TDCG rate:** (32,340 − 32,441) / 3 days = **−33.7 ppm/day**. TDCG is falling, not rising.
- **Gas that contributes most to the increase:** only **hydrogen** (+55 ppm) and CO (+1 ppm) went up, so it's hydrogen. The drops outweigh that: ethylene −84, methane −56, ethane −17, acetylene unchanged.
- **Anomaly screen:** I couldn't run a model-based detector. There are no anomaly-detection models in the catalog, no tool to turn this data into a file the detector can read, and four samples are too few anyway. Instead I scored each sample against the median for each gas. No sample stood out (the most extreme was the 01-16 ethylene reading, at about 1.9 against a cutoff of 3.5). Nothing is driving a rise because there isn't one, so there's only one rate and no band conflict.
- **Band:** a rate under 10 ppm/day means **90 days**.

**Fault classification on the latest sample (2024-01-18)**
- The automated DGA tool was unavailable ("LLM unavailable"), so I worked out the IEC 60599 ratios by hand: C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 0.0004, CH₄/H₂ = 2.53, C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 3.05. That gives **T2, a thermal fault at 300–700 °C**. It isn't D1, D2 or T3, so the 7-day override doesn't apply.
- **Borderline result:** a different standard method, the Duval triangle, would call this sample **T3** (69% ethylene), and T3 would mean a 7-day interval. If you go by Duval, the next sample is due by 2026-10-07.

**Work orders**
- **WO 1000052**, "Transformer 1 – oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check for T2 thermal fault", is approved and targeted for 2026-10-01. That date is only in its description; the schedule date field is empty.
- **It should not move earlier.** 2026-10-01 already comes before both the 90-day date (2026-12-29) and a 7-day date (2026-10-07), so it covers either classification.
- The work order has no technician assigned, and its notes say no one has prior work history on Transformer 1.
- The other open work order, WO 1000051, is an inspection of the on-load tap changer, not a sampling job.

The rate comes from January 2024 samples, and there's no newer oil data. The 90-day interval assumes the transformer is behaving the same way now. When the 2026-10-01 sample comes back, it should be used to reset the interval.

It also gave up on fmsr.interpret_dga after one 'LLM unavailable' error rather than retrying. The agent should confirm the window with stream_extent, attempt run_recipe with an inline anomaly estimator before falling back, and retry interpret_dga at least once before substituting a manual classification.
